chapter: Central High, first records and leaving home
title: Sylvester Weaver hears her at the Palace Theatre and brings Tommy Rockwell
summary: At thirteen or fourteen, playing piano and singing with the band at the Palace movie theatre, Humes was heard by blues guitarist Sylvester Weaver, who knew her father and brought record man Tommy Rockwell to hear her at home.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And he didn't go any farther? No. Well, you know you talked about that you had a little Band, all of you.
Yeah.
And you did little dates and things. And you talk about doing a session at the Palace Theatre?

Yeah, well that was a movie theatre, and they would have, you know, the band playing there. And it was there while I was playing at the Palace, that Mr. Weaver, Sylvester Weaver heard me and had Mr. Rockwell come in here and that was my first record I ever made.
How old were you at that time? Were you still at school?
Oh yeah, I was still at school. I was around thirteen or fourteen.
Oh, for goodness sake.
But I was playing with the Band, you know.
You played the piano?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yeah, I played the piano and then I'd sing.
Well, at that time would you use a megaphone?
No, I didn't need one.
You didn't need it?
No.
You could really get it out. Isn't that something. So what was Sylvester Weaver doing?
Well he was a blues singer and played the guitar.
Was he in the theatre?
No, he came to the theatre to see whatever show was going on and he heard me.
Oh.
Well, he knew my father and so, you know, he said, is it alright if he could bring . . .
Tommy Rockwell?
Yeah. So he brought him on out there and I played the piano and sang for him. And they wanted me to go the same day and make some records. So I mean, I didn't talk to him. My mother talked to him.
